findings.evidence: if collect_session_slots() can ever succeed with exactly {} (its degraded/empty payload shape is defined outside this diff), _handle_session_slots returns {} both for that success and for a failed read; the contract pins failed_read:{} so this is benign, but block_status.session_slots on /metrics is
findings.title: Successful empty block indistinguishable from failed read

findings.evidence: _refuse_read only emits logger.warning("metrics.read_refused", ...) and returns; no counter is incremented and no /metrics field records read-side refusals, so repeated 401/403/429 attempts against the reads are observable only through logs, unlike the receivers' _receiver_refused/_rejection_counter
findings.title: Read refusals are logged but never counted

findings.evidence: bucket.allow is only called (line 76) after verifier.verify, allowlist and family checks pass, so every well-formed bearer reaches the verifier unthrottled; cost is likely bounded by the registry snapshot cache (tests show reads without repo loads), but per-source limiting, if any, lives in verify()
findings.title: No throttling precedes the verifier call on the read path
